children.text: Replaces the padding list of the element toolbar

The padding select opens the box model, as the devtools draw it: the content in the middle, the padding around it with a value on each side, and around that the room the parent leaves. Every value is a step of the spacing scale, named as the class it writes, so a mixed padding reads at a glance instead of as the word mixed.
Three rings, one colour each, the same colours the canvas paints while the popover is open.
Its size and how it is sized: hug, fill or fixed. Read only; the size is Design mode's.
A value on each side. Click one to pick it, ⌘-click to pick several, then choose a step and every side picked takes it; or drag a value up or down, or use the arrows.
There is no margin in a page: the room between an element and its siblings is its parent's gap, on the axis the parent stacks. Its values set the parent's gap, and the note says whose.
What is written, in Tailwind's words. The trigger shows the same values in CSS order: top, right, bottom, left.

Hold ⌘ and click sides to pick them together, in any mode. The scale then sets every side picked: while their values differ, the steps they use are ringed and none is filled; one click on a step makes them all that step. The classes collapse to the shortest Tailwind form.
Picks one side, and drops the others.
Adds a side, or takes it out of the pick.
Drops the pick; the scale hides.
All, X · Y and Sides decide how many values the box asks for. Changing the mode keeps what is set: going from Sides to All takes the side picked. The trigger shortens to match.

While the popover is open the element is painted as the devtools paint it: its padding green, the gap to its siblings amber. The side under the pointer, in the popover or on the canvas, is painted stronger and measured; dragging a side's edge on the canvas walks the same scale.
